text: Since the designation of a "word" (pada) has been prescribed by Panini (1.4.14) and by Gautama (Nyaya Sutra 2.2.60), the word will be perceived in the letters themselves by adhering to the convention and for the sake of convenience. Therefore, the number of letters in the word "sara" is the same as in "rasa." If it is argued that in cases such as "vana" and "nava," "nadi" and "dina," "rama" and "mara," "raja" and "jara," there would be no perception of a difference in meaning, then that is not the case, because the difference arises from the difference in the order of the letters.
